subject: Post-call: POC scope & recommended model + language fallback plan
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Aditi Shah <aditi.shah@optiretail.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@optiretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: POC scope & recommended model + language fallback plan

Thanks again for the time earlier today — great alignment on the core use case (customer support triage + automated first-touch replies for high-frequency SKUs). Below is a concise recap, our recommended POC approach for model selection and language handling, success criteria we agreed to, and proposed next steps.

Summary of what we heard
- Goal: reduce time-to-first-response and deflect common queries while keeping escalations accurate for agents.
- Volume profile: 4–6k daily interactions; peak spikes during promos (2x baseline).
- Target locales for Phase 1: en-US, es-ES, pt-BR (catalog & customer messages).

Recommended POC approach (short):
1) Baseline model (hosted): Mistral-Instruct-7B quantized (8-bit) — good latency, strong instruction following for short replies, lower cost.
2) Fallback model (higher-quality for ambiguous/long-context): Llama-2-13B-chat (fp16 on dedicated pool) — used for longer threads or when safety/clarity score below threshold.
3) Multilingual handling: run a language-detection step; for es/pt we will evaluate two paths in the POC: (A) native responses from the selected model variants if performance meets accuracy threshold; (B) translate-to-en -> model -> translate-back for the highest-safety paths if native quality lags. We'll instrument both to compare.
4) Caching & routing: prefix caching for common SKU questions and a KV cache for recent context to keep token cost down.

Proposed POC success criteria (we'll measure these against the eval set in attachments):
- Accuracy (intent+slot correctness) >= 85% on sample eval prompts for each language.
- Hallucination rate < 2% as measured by explicit hallucination checks.
- Response latency p50 < 250ms for baseline path, p95 < 800ms overall (including fallback).
- Deflection rate >= 30% (percent of interactions fully handled without agent follow-up).
- Safety/regression: zero critical safety regressions across the eval set (we will run red-team subset).

Operational assumptions & cost knobs
- Start POC on hosted shared capacity for speed of onboarding; escalate to a short dedicated pool if we hit sustained peak load in week 2 of the POC.
- We'll provide an initial cost estimate (see attached PDF) with options for 50/100/200 concurrent tokens to show run-rate.

Owners (proposed)
- Redwood Sales/Primary: Marcus Lin — POC coordination, SoW and commercial kickoff.
- Redwood Solutions: Ben Carter — model tuning, eval harness, and infra config (batching / cache / quantization profiles).
- Redwood Customer Success: Monica Patel — success metrics owner, runbook, acceptance tests.
- Legal/Finance: Laura Bennett — SoW and billing.

Next steps (proposed calendar)
- 09/03: Redwood to share eval prompt set + success metric spreadsheet (attached).
- 09/06: OptiRetail to confirm any additional non-functional requirements (data residency, audit logs).
- 09/08: POC kickoff (1 week baseline + optional week extension) — target completion 09/15 (report back).

Attachments: optiretail-poc-success-metrics.xlsx, eval-prompts-EN-ES-PT.csv, poc-timeline-and-costs.pdf

Thanks — I captured these items quickly while fresh, happy to update based on your notes.

—Marcus

- Evaluation sets: can you confirm the Spanish prompts are es-ES vs en-ES (we need to make sure colloquial phrasings are covered)?
- Data residency: we need logs retained in our EU GCP project for audit; is that possible in the hosted flow or will that force us to Private deployment for the POC?
- Cost clarity: for the two-model approach (Mistral baseline + Llama-2 fallback), can you give a ballpark incremental cost for adding the fallback model during weeks with 2x peak?

If those are manageable we'll confirm 09/08 kickoff. Also copied Tom — he requested a short SoW draft to review.

Subject: Re: Post-call: POC scope & recommended model + language fallback plan

Quick answers to Aditi's questions: 
- Spanish locale: we'll include both es-ES and a small en-ES subset in the eval prompts (we'll tag prompts by region+register). The CSV attached has a column for locale; we'll expand if you point to any customer samples.
- Data residency for POC: hosted flow can keep logs in your EU project if you choose our EU-hosted tenancy (we can set a temporary private bucket with object-level retention rules). If you require on-prem or fully private control of keys for the POC, that triggers Redwood Private and adds ~5 business days for setup. For initial testing the EU-hosted tenancy should be fine.
- Cost for fallback during 2x peaks: rough estimate: baseline (Mistral-7B quantized) ~ $0.12 / 1k tokens; fallback (Llama-2-13B fp16 on dedicated) adds approx $0.45 / 1k tokens when used. With routing thresholds, we expect fallback to trigger ~15% of tokens in peak scenarios; that maps to roughly +20–25% run-rate during peak weeks. We'll produce a tighter estimate in the attached poc-timeline-and-costs.pdf.

Proposed timeline (more granular):
- 09/03: Redwood share eval set + SoW draft. (Marcus)
- 09/06: OptiRetail returns any privacy / compliance must-haves. (Aditi)
- 09/08: Kickoff — day 0 baseline config: eval harness deployed, baseline model live behind a test route, telemetry wired to your EU bucket. (Ben / Monica)
- 09/08–09/14: Run evaluation (daily ingest, collect metrics, iterate on prompts & caching). (Ben)
- 09/15: Team demo + acceptance check against spreadsheet. (All)

I'll own the first-pass model configs and will include the quantization profile and batching settings in the first commit. Monica will set up the acceptance dashboards.

—Ben
